newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Record Australia barley crop of 6 mln T seen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Record Australia barley crop of 6 mln T seen.

text.p: Australia's official commodities forecasting agency said on Tuesday Australian barley production was estimated at a record 6.0 million tonnes in 1996/97, 10 percent higher than last year's crop.
The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said the increase was a result of the combination of increased plantings and higher yields across most states.
In its latest crop report, ABARE said that in New South Wales mild spring temperatures and regular rains had led to a largely favourable end to the season.

Despite some adverse weather conditions in the north of the state, overall state yields had been largely unaffected and early indications were for an above average proportion of the state's production being classified as malting quality, it said.
New South Wales production was estimated at 1.2 million tonnes, 36 percent above last year's level.
ABARE said in Western Australia, barley production was estimated to be around 1.4 million tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March), 10 percent higher than last season.

A dry finish to the season in a number of northern and central inland areas had resulted in higher than usual protein levels and, as a result, a reduced proportion of the crop was expected to be graded as malting quality, it said.
However, for the later maturing crops in the south of the state, late rain had assisted grain filling, it said.

ABARE said in South Australia the absence of rain damage to date in most ripened crops was promising in terms of quality but with harvest not being well underway until late November, there was still significant uncertainty over crop quality, it said.
Leaf rust had been widely reported and was serious in some crops, particularly in the south of the Yorke Peninsula, the major barley producing region, it said.
South Australian production was estimated to be 1.9 million tonnes in 1996/97, the same level as harvested in 1995/96, it said.
